skill.name: hooks-management
skill.description: Create, configure, validate, and troubleshoot Claude Code hooks using bundled reference docs and a security-focused workflow.
skill.summary: Guides safe Claude Code hook creation, validation, and troubleshooting.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: I adjudicated all 52 static findings as false positives because they occur in Markdown code spans or reference examples, not executable skill code. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious hook behavior was found. The skill remains security-sensitive by purpose because it helps create Claude Code hooks, so user review should stay visible.

remediation.issue: Credential placeholder in a reference example
remediation.suggestion: Replace API_KEY with a non-secret placeholder and direct users to approved secret storage for real credentials.

remediation.issue: Hook changes can affect future Claude Code execution
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before writing hook scripts or settings, and show changed paths before completion.

remediation.issue: Shell examples may be copied into active hooks
remediation.suggestion: Prefer Python templates for generated hooks and add command allowlists, input validation, and timeouts.

static_findings.snippet: 2. **Verify syntax** - Ensure your JSON settings are valid
- Hooks can modify, delete, or access any files your user account can access
- Review existing hooks in `.claude/hooks/` and settings in `.claude/settings.local.json`
- Verify hook execution using `echo` to pipe JSON input

content.value_statement: Claude Code hooks are powerful but easy to configure incorrectly. This skill guides hook creation, validation, and troubleshooting with security checks.
actual_capabilities: Reads bundled hook documentation and input pattern references.
Reviews existing .claude/hooks scripts and local hook settings.
Creates or updates Claude Code hook scripts for supported events.
Tests hook execution with representative JSON input through echo.
Checks hook scripts for security, error handling, and loop risks.
Reports hook status and validation results to the main agent.
limitations: Does not make unsafe hook commands safe by itself.
Relies on the bundled documentation matching the installed Claude Code version.
Should not manage secrets, tokens, or critical system files.
Requires user review before enabling hooks that run automatically.

use_cases.title: Add a Project Hook
use_cases.description: Create a hook that runs formatting or validation after file edits in a project.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Automation
use_cases.description: Review hook settings and align event coverage across shared development workflows.

use_cases.title: Audit Existing Hooks
use_cases.description: Inspect hook scripts for unsafe commands, missing validation, and loop risks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple project automation hook.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code hook that runs our existing formatter after Write and Edit events. Include testing and safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Hook Inputs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate validation for event payload handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my hook input handling for malformed data, missing fields, and clear error reporting. Suggest focused fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Failing Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate debugging for a hook that does not run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose why my Claude Code hook is not triggering. Check matcher names, settings syntax, command paths, and permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure Hook Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for several hooks across events.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure hook strategy for validation, notifications, and session setup. Include threat risks and rollout steps.

output_examples.input: Create a hook that validates changed Markdown files after edits.
output_examples.output: A hook plan with event selection, matcher scope, script location, validation behavior, test steps, and enablement notes.

output_examples.input: Review an existing hook that blocks unsafe shell commands.
output_examples.output: An audit summary covering command parsing, blocked patterns, exit behavior, error messages, and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot a hook that does not run on file writes.
output_examples.output: A diagnostic report covering settings placement, matcher names, executable permissions, command paths, and debug log checks.

best_practices: Keep hook commands narrow, explicit, and easy to review.
Validate input fields before reading paths or running commands.
Test hooks in a safe project before enabling them broadly.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding credentials or tokens in hook scripts.
Auto-approving sensitive actions without clear user review.
Writing hooks that can trigger themselves repeatedly.

faq.question: What does this skill help manage?
faq.answer: It helps create, update, validate, and troubleshoot Claude Code hooks and related local settings.

faq.question: Does it execute hooks automatically?
faq.answer: The skill guides hook creation and testing. Claude Code executes enabled hooks according to the user configuration.

faq.question: Can it work with existing hook scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review existing scripts and settings before proposing targeted updates.

faq.question: Is it safe for secrets?
faq.answer: No. Hook scripts should not hardcode credentials, tokens, or private keys.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users review before enabling hooks?
faq.answer: Users should review changed files, command paths, input validation, timeouts, and any automatic approval behavior.
